# Server-produced machine files

Twelve machine files emitted by the **Tamga server's own `encode_machine_file`**
(`tamga-api`, `src/shared/crypto/machine_file.rs`), copied here byte-for-byte.
Nothing in this repository produced any of them, and nothing here may
regenerate them.

`tests/integration/server_machine_files_test.c` drives the whole set from
`manifest.json`, so a file added to this directory with a manifest entry is
exercised without editing the test.

## Why they exist

`tests/fixtures/offline/` is generated by `tools/fixture-generator/` — by this
repository, for this repository. Every machine file in it is offline format
**v1** (`alg` of `base64+ed25519`, no `+v2`), and its encrypted variant packs
`nonce||ciphertext||tag` into a single base64 blob. The server has emitted
neither shape for two years:

| | what this SDK generated and tested against | what the server actually emits |
|---|---|---|
| `alg` | `base64+ed25519` | `base64+ed25519+v2` |
| encrypted `enc` | `base64(nonce‖ct‖tag)` | `base64(nonce) "." base64(ct‖tag)` |
| signed payload | `{data}` | `{data, meta:{iat,exp,jti,kid}}` |

Because the generator and the verifier shared one misreading of the format, CI
stayed green while no build of this SDK could open a single real file. These
fixtures are the fix for that, and it is the reason they must not be
regenerated locally: a fixture this repository produces proves only that the
code agrees with itself.

## Parameters

Licence key `TAMGA-FIXTURE-LICENSE-KEY-0001`, machine fingerprint
`fixture-fingerprint-a1b2c3`. Each manifest entry carries its own
`public_key_b64`, `kid`, `scheme`, `alg`, `encrypted`, `enc_is_dot_separated`,
`license_key`, `fingerprint` and `expired`.

Four signing schemes × three variants:

| variant | `alg` | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<scheme>_plain_valid` | `base64+<suffix>+v2` | `exp` one hour after `iat` |
| `<scheme>_encrypted_valid` | `aes-256-gcm+<suffix>+v2` | `enc` is dot-separated |
| `<scheme>_plain_expired` | `base64+<suffix>+v2` | `exp` one hour *before* `iat` |

Signing suffixes: `ed25519`, `ecdsa-p256`, `rsa-sha256` (PKCS#1 v1.5) and
`rsa-pss-sha256`. Note that `rsa-sha256` is what the server emits for
`Rsa2048Pkcs1Sign` **and** for `Rsa2048JwtRs256` — the suffix cannot identify
the scheme, which is why the caller supplies it and the file's `alg` is only a
cross-check.

The RSA public keys are PKCS#1 `RSAPublicKey` DER; the ECDSA one is a 65-byte
uncompressed point; the Ed25519 one is 32 raw bytes.

## ⚠️ The "valid" fixtures expire

They were issued with a **one-hour ttl**, so their `exp` is one hour after the
moment they were generated. Any test that verifies them against the wall clock
begins failing an hour later.

`tamga_machine_file_verify_at()` exists for exactly this: the test reads each
file's own signed `iat`/`exp` back out of it and checks the expiry boundary
against those, which is stable forever. Do not reach for
`tamga_machine_file_verify()` (the public wrapper, which reads the local
clock) in a test that expects one of these to verify.

## Regenerating

Don't. If a case is missing, ask for it to be produced from the server's
encoder and copied in. A fixture written here by hand — or by
`tools/fixture-generator/` — reproduces whatever this SDK currently believes,
which is the exact failure these files exist to close.

No private keys are committed; only the public halves, inside `manifest.json`.
